topic: What if you got a five-star wanted level in real life?

script.text: At first, it's a game, and you're very good at it. On Wednesday, you drop a candy wrapper outside the bakery. One star. Somewhere, a radio crackles.

Ninety seconds later, an officer on a bicycle comes round the corner, looking left, looking right. You step behind a bus shelter, and you count. The star flashes, then it's gone. The officer shrugs and rides away.
You pick up the wrapper and put it in the trash. Mo saw the whole thing. 'Okay,' he says. 'What just happened?'
So you show him. You walk on the grass, right next to the sign that says Keep Off. One star. And there's the officer again, right on time, like a bus. Mo nearly falls over.
It's always the same officer. Officer Dale. He has a moustache, and a bicycle bell he rings when he's annoyed. By the third time, he just sighs and waves.
Mo wants a go too. He drops a wrapper, walks on the grass, even stands in the middle of the road until a lady with a dog tells him off. Nothing. No stars. It only works on you.
By Thursday, Mo is writing it all down in a notebook. 'Library book, three days late. One star. Skateboard in the parking lot. One star. Running away from one star. Two stars.'
Two stars means a patrol car. Real lights, a real siren, and a real officer who looks very confused about why he has been sent to a parking lot because of a skateboard.
You duck into the laundromat and sit between two old ladies reading magazines. The stars flash, and fade. The car drives away.
On the way home, you practise. One star, hide, count, fade. One star, hide, count, fade. You're getting fast. Your record is twenty-eight seconds.
'This is the best thing that has ever happened to anyone,' says Mo. And for one more day, you believe him.
